children.title: Four planes of development and education

blocks.text: What is human development?
Maria Montessori said that it is a process of becoming which takes time. The goal is to reach the state of adulthood.
We can describe the adult as an independent being which is self-sufficient. We as human beings take a longer time than the other species to reach independence.
The goal of development is to become adult with all its characteristics (L’uomo). This goal comes from within, as something given by nature as this energy can’t come from outside.
We should always keep in mind that the child is not an empty vessel to be filled or a block of stone to be sculpted by someone else.

Maria Montessori classifies the developmental processes as natural, and can be viewed in two ways. “Finality” is the intrinsic element of a child and from the outside element there is the “causalistic” component (cause and effect).

The laws of development are disclosed by the child and are revealed with the help of observation. The behaviour of a child can’t be interpreted with the “causalistic” thinking of the adult. The behaviour has to be interpreted in a way in which it helps the child, by looking at the behaviour and understanding its goal.

It is very important to put in focus the child, as they are the future. Unfortunately in today’s society the “the child is the forgotten citizen” (Maria Montessori). The adults should behave as the ambassador of the children, as the “causalistic” component it is very important for the development of the child and it is the responsibility of the adult. We, the adults, are responsible for the conditions in the environment and we should remove the obstacles/barriers that hinder the development of the child.
Maria Montessori describes the birth as an entrance in a new world. She calls the energy at the birth: “the nebulae”. “Nebulae” means possibility, a potential to transform something into reality.

When talking about the development of the child we can’t talk of lineal development, instead we can talk about planes or stages of development each with its own requirements, interests of the human being and challenges. The adult can’t rush the passage from one plane to the other. We can consider the passage from a plane of development to the other as a rebirth.

A quick explanation of the chart called “The four planes of development” – The “Constructive rhythm of life”: Colours: Maria Montessori chose the red fire for the birth of the child, bold red line for the growth planes and blue thin lines for the calm and uniform development. In contrast in the lower part it is represented in grey the lineal educational program available for the children in the traditional schools. Symbols: The horizontal arrow with the word “Finality” showing towards the goal of the development: the adulthood. In the lower part the vertical, upward showing arrows represent the number of teachers that a child has during the school years. The horizontal lines in tha last block represent the various types of studies available to choose towards the maturity.

children.title: The first plane – the construction of the self

blocks.text: The first years of life are the most important. If before birth we can talk about the physical embryo, in the first three years of life Maria Montessori talk about a spiritual embryo. In this first three years of life we can observe the development of the equilibrium, the development of the hand and the development of the language. These different human powers develop independently but work unites them in the development and any external obstruction can become and internal obstacle. The children need to function in a context, mind and body in a harmonious fashion.

Between the age of 0 and 3 years old we can observe the basic acquisition of movement, sensorial powers(perception) and language. Maria Montessori calls these sensitive periods. Also at this age exists a sensitivity for order as movement, perception and language all have order. The children need order (both temporal and spatial) in their environment and routines to help them develop their maximum potential. The lack of order and routine might create a sense of insecurity in the child.
“A place for everything and everything in its place” Maria Montessori

In the first years of life there is a process of adaption to the environment where the child was born, the child will learn from the environment and from the group that surrounds him. So he and the environment are at harmony.

The child will learn more in the first three years of life than in the rest of his life. This is why it is of critical importance to make sure that in these period he is surrounded by an environment without obstacles, with rich and engaging activities for his age and needs.
Between the ages of 3 and 6 years old we can talk about a refinment of that basic acquisitions from the previous stage, a constructive perfectionment.

In this stage the child will work to perfect the skills developed in the first three years of life. Maria Montessori talks about “an absorbent mind” in this first plane of development which allows the child to absorb all that surrounds him.
Mario Montessori called the children in the first plane of development: “Sensorial Motor Explorers”.
The second plane of development – a calm phase of uniform

children.title: The second plane of development – a calm phase of uniform growth

blocks.text: By the time the child enters in the second plane of development they are very much already formed as individuals. The second plane is important but not so formative as the first one. Now the interest of the child is thrown outward to the world and universe. He requires an open environment to represent his interests and feed the hungry mind.
At this stage we can talk about three kinds of sensitivity:
 Sensitivity for the acquision of culture The child is hungry for knowledge and understanding asking questions such as “How ?” and “Why?”. The child wants to understand the world where he is living.
 Sensitivity for imagination
The senses are not enough for the second plane child as at this stage using only
the senses they might be lead to the wrong answers. Imagination is required to
picture realities that otherwise can not be accessed. (for example dinosaurs,
microscopic realities or even the universe).
Some of the elementary material is called an Aid to Imagination. In this second
plane the imagination is used to talk about the reality. Maria Montessori called this type of imagination “the eyes of the mind”.

 Sensitivity for morality Here we talk about morality in the context of the human being being able to live together. If in the first plane of development the child absorbs the natural environment with all the morality, value systems and religion, in the seond plane of development they are going to question what surrounds them, including the rules and the values of the society. If the rules in the Children’s House are intended as a form of respect for the others and not debatable , in Elementary the rules can be discussed with the children and a consent has to be reached as it should be a community of equals. Maria Montessori said that this sensitivity is where they are most vulnerable and where we should take a lot of care.

If in the Children’s house there are certain group activities like “walking on the line”, but they are not as systematic as in the elementary. Now their interest shifts from their family to their friends and peers. It is an age where they form groups (gregarious instinct) where they come up with their own rules, their secret language or signs, all being part of the natural development.
Mario Montessori says the magnetism is orientated towards friends instead of family.
Their characteristics have a natural purspose and are not permanent. The children in this second plane are trying to create a small pretend society.
As the social aspect is permanent in the human being we do not call it a sensitivity.
Between the age of 6 and 12 years old the children tend to associate between themselves and not so much with the adult.
We can consider this period as a great moment for the intelectual exploration.

children.title: The third plane of development – “Let’s help us to do it by ourselves”

blocks.text: ourselves”

The third plane of development is a growth plane in which take place the transformations of the child into an adult. In this creative plane the child experiences a physical growth during puberty. Now the individual is more vulnerable and prone to disease. It is a moment of the development of the secondary sexual characteristics. The adolescent is very self-consciuous, as this is a moment when they get to consider and asset their reality and capacities. In this plane the adolescent needs encouragement to pursue their interests.

Maria Montessori proposed for the education of the adolescent the Farm Schools. A place in which they can engage in outdoor activities, self-expression activities but also study. In the first three years of this plane, we can call the adolescent between 12 and 15, the new born adult. They have a high interest to participate in the adult society. In the third plane of development there is a sensitivity for the persanal dignity and a sensitivity of a sense of justice.

children.title: The forth plane of development – maturity

blocks.text: The brain continues to develop till the age of 24. It is the frontal lobe which is responsibile for the decision making, the one that develops the most. At different ages we can talk of different kinds of independence:
 Mental (0-6 years old)  Moral (values) (6-12 years old)  Economic (12-18 years old)  Spiritual (18-24 years old)
Descriptions that we can give to the stages of development:

 0-3 years old: Spiritual embryo ( Formation of man)  3-6 years old: Constructive perfectionsm (Mobel Kinder) – Blessed age of play ( as they always do things with their hands)  6-12 years old: Age of rudeness (quite self-asserted)  12-18: Erd Kinder (Farm school)  18-24: Age of hapiness
In the Montessori education we can talk about different planes of education:  0-6 years old: The home  6-12 years old: Cosmic education  12-18 years old: The land
We need enlightened love fo the child, allowing the development by himself. The children are natural learners and the educational process has more to do with this natural desire than with teaching.
The chart above is called the “The four planes of development” – The “bulb”. This is a
more organic representation of the four stages of development. Starting from the
nebulae (the potential of development of the new born) and going towards the
Finality: “The man”. In this chart in the traditional education the “crèche” and the pre-
school are included but we observe still a single great plane of education with the
goal “the degree”.
The “X” stands for “man the unknown”, as we still don’t know how the man and society
will be if we don’t obstruct the development of the individual.
In Maria Montessori’s books there is no chapter or article related to the human tendencies, as she was talking about it late in her life. It was left to Mario Montessori to talk about it.
The sensitivities have a rising path and then a descending one, giving space to the next sensitivities of the next plane of development.
The human tendencies are found only through the process of development.

Early in her writings Maria Montessori tried to show the differences between the children and adults by contrasting them in their behaviour and actions. When we have to talk about the human tendencies we have to talk about what we all share. Human tendencies are characteristic to all human beings, to adults and children as well. They are universal.

Mario Montessori tries to help the adults to understand the children by finding these tendencies in himself. The sensitive periods apply to a very limited amount of time, at a specific moment, meanwhile the tendencies last for the whole life.
We can start by considering life as a whole. When we consider the coming to life we speak of the commands of life (eat, grow, and make others as yourself).
Each form of life has its own way of life, normally in relation with a particular environment. What it is that makes a creature behave in a specific way?

We can think of plants for example. They have sensitivities called tropisms. Plants have phototropism (it will grow towards light), geotropism (its roots will grow towards the centre of Earth) and hydrotropism (it will grow towards the water). Plants cannot decide if they will obey or not their sensitivities. Plants are like a bridge between a non- living world and the living world. They are the only one that make their own food. Even if there many different species of plants, their path of development it is predetermined in the seed and each plants grows following the pattern found in the seed.

When we talk about animals we talk about instincts. Each creature has a specific way of life. An animal left to itself doesn’t have the freedom to live something other than a good animal life. He will grow according to the pattern of that species.

All the human beings constitute only one species. If we think about the human beings around the world they have different ways of life around the world. It makes a very big difference where you live on the planet.

Because the human beings live in these different territories they have developed different ways of life and have different customs, beliefs, morals and so on. Each group has its own spiritual territory.
The children in a group take all these characteristics of the spiritual territory through the adults in their group and the environment that surrounds them.
Not only might the human the groups as a whole differ from one another, but also the individuals in the group develop differently. The individual differences reveal in

different kinds of work. This means there is nothing predetermined in a way the child is born. The new-borns of now and those born ten thousand years ago are the same and we can talk about the same potentials and same work of development.

It is the environment where the child finds himself that determines the identity of the child. The child constructs himself as an individual of a specific time and place and member of a specific culture. When it comes to adaption we can think of this as a work of development in the first plane.

Without tropism or instincts (animals), the human beings have the tendencies to help them guide themselves in the development. We can think of the human tendencies as a natural/genetic inclination or predisposition.
Unlike the absorbent mind these human tendencies are found during the whole life irrespective of age, so we can find them in children and adults as well.
“Tendencies do not change and human tendencies are hereditary, the child possess them in potentiality at birth and makes use of them to build an individual
suited to his time” Mario Montessori
Adults are fully developed beings while children are still in the process of development. Development unfolds in four planes with each of their distinctive characteristics.
“During the period of human growth, these tendencies assume different aspects by the aid of what doctor Montessori called sensitive periods. It is logical that if one can

discover tendencies and sensitive periods and one is able to second them, he will have found a secure and permanent foundation on which to base education, if education is viewed as a help to fulfil the potential of the child” Mario Montessori
We should always think of education as a help to life, a way to help each individual to reach his potential.
In Montessori education we put development at the centre and not the curriculum at the centre. This is why we have to understand well the sensitive periods and the human tendencies.
“Something new came into the world with man, a psychic energy of life different from any that had yet been expressed” Maria Montessori
Maria Montessori speaks not only of the biosphere but also of the psychic sphere. She speaks about the human race as living also in a supernature (the environment build by the man).
“The animal has a small physique that serves the body, while the human has a small body that serves a great physique.” Mario Montessori
The human beings have different kinds of needs not only material. They have needs also in relation with the physique: the spiritual needs (culture and art, religion and vanity).
No one can predict how a baby can develop and what he will become. It is more an individual pattern than a species pattern. The child is in harmony with the environment,
he and the environment are one. He receives a lot of help from nature (the absorbent mind, the sensitive periods and the human tendencies).
Human tendencies:

It has to do with finding ones bearings, to orientate in space and in its environment. It’s a process of building a mind map that helps us to orientate. Orientation depends on order/stability of the environment. Nature gives a certain constancy but we cannot say the same thing about the human environment. We can understand the sensitivity for order if we first understand the tendency to orientate oneself. The ability to orientate gives security and mastery and frees for exploring.

“Nature gives small children an intrinsic sensibility to order, as built up by an inner sense which is a sense not of distinction between things but of distinction of the relationship between things, so that it perceives an environment as a whole with interdependent parts. Only in such an environment, known as a whole, is it possible for the child to orient himself and to act with purpose; without it he would have no basis on which to build his perception of relationship. It would be like having furniture without a house to put it in. What would be the use of an accumulation of external images without the order that brings them into organised relation? If man knew only separate objects and not their relations, he would find himself in an inextricable confusion. It is to the child's labours that man owes the faculty, which seems a gift of nature of orienting himself, of finding his way about, in the world. In the sensitive period of order, nature gives the first lesson, in the same way as a teacher will show a child a plan of the classroom, to prepare him for the study of geographical maps. Or we may say that by this first lesson nature has given man a compass to orient him in the world. In the same way she gives the small child the power of exact reproduction of the sounds that make up language, that language that is capable of infinite development, and which the adult will evolve through the ages. Man's mind does not spring from nothing; is built up on the foundations laid by the child in his sensitive periods.”
Maria Montessori – The secret of childhood
For children every place is an unknown place and there so they need order to orientate.
“When we lose our sense of orientation we don’t simply feel physically lost, we feel lost in our mind” Mario Montessori

For the second plane child the open environment is much bigger, but he would like to explore even the biggest environment of all: the universe. When we have orientation we can explore further and further, so the environment in which we orientate expands. It means that we have an expanding environment in which we can find ourselves with confidence and security. The young child of the first plane it is in this limited environment (the family, the house) but the second plane child can explore further (the town or the

surroundings of his place). We don’t talk of a sense of order in the second plane of development but for the exploration of more knowledge the child needs order. When we offer to the children the cosmic fables in elementary, it helps them to find a first orientation.
“The cosmic education gives the child an orientation and guidance in life” Maria Montessori

Exploration means setting venture into the unknown to discover or to understand something new. The tendency to explore is connected to the curiosity. For explorations it is very important to be sure where we are, so orientation is a requisite for satisfactory exploration. Without orientation the exploration might become just meaningless wandering. Exploring it helps the human beings discover whatever it is required to satisfy their human needs. We have explored all the aspects of our natural environment always driven by our needs. The humans start with a certain physical environment and slowly expand, adapting and creating even a spiritual territory. The first plane children explore the immediate environment, perceptible to the senses. Through explorations the unknown world in which he entered becomes known. The second plane children are not only attracted to the immediate environment and as they want to explore a more extended environment (the society, the world and the universe). The reality is still being explored but not the one so tangible only with the senses. None of these realities can be explored only with the senses as it requires the power of imagination (“the eyes of the mind”). Now the child needs a different kind of help, he needs to orientate through stories and key lessons. It helps to mention also the exploration of the moral and social aspects of the life. The third plane adolescent is interested to explore the adult world of work and the society.

To orientate and to explore are related and also we can say the same thing about to observe. Observation should be connected with all the senses not only the sight. To observe we can think of it as an exploration with the senses. The more acute are the senses the easier is to observe. Observation is a way to get impressions of the environment. The little child in the first year of life observes everything around him and tastes everything. Everything the child comes in contact with he will absorb it. During the second year of life the child starts observing the small objects and the

details, sometimes so small, almost invisible. Between the ages of 3 to 6 the child is refining the skills of observation. As the child enhances his powers of observation, the world becomes a richer place. In this way the mind becomes more prepared for what it will come later. The second plane child is capable of looking at the reality with different eyes. (E.g. observing the leaves in different ways at different ages.) The child is ready to observe in a new way when the mind is prepared to see a different reality, with the eyes of understanding. As the child grows older he becomes more aware and starts reasoning in a more abstract way. The mind that looks through the relationship between cause and effect. We can say that knowledge begins with the power to observe. If we observe nature with a reasoning mind we can find answers to our needs. Human beings observed many things in nature and then reproduced them in supernature. Observation can be an important force for creation.

To abstract – etymologically is “to draw off from”. By having various experiences the child can extract the idea of an object/concept. Once you have the abstraction of an object you don’t depend on the experience itself. Language it is by its nature an abstraction. In the process that leads to abstraction, the imagine that it’s part of the process it is in service of the tendency to abstract. Imagination helps the tendency of abstraction. There is always a passage from what it is concrete to abstract, but the mind has to make the passage with the help of the experience. Not everyone finds it easy the passage to abstraction. Without the power of abstraction it would be impossible to create new things in our supernature. Second plane children enter the plane of abstract, as they can work at a more abstract level in their mind. There are many levels of abstraction:
Abstraction of a real object
Abstraction of a quality Abstraction of a number

Imagination is the ability to form images in the mind. It is possible to imagine things that we already seen but also things that can be seen with the “eyes of the mind” which don’t exist or that have been seen before. The imagination that Maria Montessori talks about is connected to reality. The creative imagination it is very important for the second plane child as it allows them to travel in time and space. The reality that we might know it can be used in the service of the abstraction and finally use the abstraction in the service of the imagination (e.g. imagining a desert with the help of description of realities that we know). The first plane child acquires many abstractions and the

second plane child uses those in order to make use of the imagination. Imagination helped the humanity to evolve and to progress. Without the help of imagination the humans couldn’t build the supernature. Every time we think about different civilizations we use the power of imagination.

children.title: To work (to be active, to move, to manipulate, to experience through oneself)

blocks.text: oneself)

Work is an activity with a purpose. All the work that we offer it commits the children to having experiences. To bring imagination into reality it requires work. If we look throughout the history then we will realise that there is a story of work. The human beings are workers – “the human beings are born to work.” Maria Montessori

The children have this incredible human tendency to work. There are differences between the work of the adult and the child’s work. The adult work laws are the “law of the division of labour” and the “law of minimum effort”. The purpose of the adult is to change the environment and this is a tiring work.

A prepared environment has to be used for the purpose of giving the child a place where he can use his natural energy to create and perfect himself. The child is also a worker and a producer and it has the task of producing “the man”. The child’s labour we can say it is opposed to the one of the adult, it is a creative labour. The child’s work uses the environment to transform the child itself as opposed to what the adult uses the work for. The adult is the one preparing the environment but it is the child who is the using the environment to perfect himself.

“The child does not follow the law of the least effort, but a law directly contrary. He wastes an immense amount of energy over an unsubstantial end, and he wastes not only driving energy but intensive, energy in the exact execution of every detail.” Maria Montessori – The secret of the childhood

The point is not the product but the process because the product is himself. The child is not externally motivated it is internally motivated. The child uses the environment but for personal purposes. The adult is exhausted of his work but the child is refreshed.
“(…) a distinction must be made between work and forced labour. The outer
appearance might be the same, but the former is of a spirit that finds its
expression in activity, whereas the latter is a burden that deadens and
crushed any spirituality one may possess and fosters resistance, rebellion,
resentment and hatred.” Mario Montessori –
India, 1948
Young children work to understand meanwhile a second plane child must understand before starting to work. Work is the most important tool towards the “normalization”/healing of the child.

The brain is a concentration of nervous cells (neurons). Movement helps the development of the brain and is crucial especially for the young children. The first plane children have the opportunity to move as almost all the activities presented in Children’s house have a component of movement.

To be exact means to be precise. As soon as the human being interacts with reality a certain degree of exactness is required. All the inventions and discoveries need a level of exactness. This tendency keeps us working and improving ourselves. In this sense exactness and control of error are coming together in the Montessori materials. Some of the sensorial materials in the Children’s House require a high amount of exactness. The humans have a mathematical mind, and whenever we think about mathematics there two words that come to our mind: order and exactness.

“What was forgotten was to give exactness to the children. The importance of this detail was not understood, but it is the centre of everything. It is from this that there comes activity, joy, work, perfectionment. The point is not to render a person exact in the usual way of acting, tied to details instead of to the whole, it is to render the mind capable of seeing. Without which capacity one remains blind, grows in a blind way, when the details of exactness, which gave such brilliant results in the beginning are neglected there comes about decadence in our education even if gran ideas are dawn by theory”. Maria
Montessori’s letter to her former student Giuliana Sorge
“In our tiny children the evidence of a mathematical bent shows itself in many striking and spontaneous ways.

In fact, if we showed them exactly how to do something, this precision itself seemed to hold their interest. To have a real purpose to which the action was directed, this was the first condition, but the exact way of doing it acted like a support which rendered the child stable in his efforts, and therefore brought
him to make progress in his development. Order and precision, we found, were the keys to spontaneous work in the school.

And if we look now at the sensorial apparatus which is able to evoke such deep concentration (remarkable in very small children between the ages of three and four), there is no doubt that this apparatus may be regarded not only as a help to exploring the environment, but also to the development of
the mathematical mind.” Maria Montessori – The Absorbent Mind

Second plane children seek knowledge and understanding of the world, and there is where exactness is required. We can help the children to imagine by giving him this exactness in our descriptions. For the mathematics in Elementary we have the mathematical aids so that the children can picture reality exactly. The second plane children also will look for the exactness in morality and the rules of the society.

It is very wrong to think that to calculate it is strictly connected to mathematics. We calculate all the time in our daily life, in order to move, to manipulate objects, to navigate, to explore or to observe. The control of error comes from the environment that surrounds us. The young children have to make an effort to calculate the precise movements of the body. The adults in order to calculate developed many instruments that come as aids.

To repeat means to do an activity/action more than one time. For any new ability that the humans want to master, repetition is required. Practice in sports, dance, art, music called practice in fact is just a form of repetition for improving the skills in that area. When the children are very small, repetition not only help them to master some skills but also helps them to develop their muscular strength. Once the ability is acquired then repetition is not necessary anymore. In the second plane children we cannot expect this repetition to take place in the same manner as with the first plane children. Talent can be polished only with repetition and the ones who reach high professional levels are the ones who put many hours in getting better and better.

It is a tendency to improve oneself at some activity. There is always going to be room for improvement but this road brings intrinsic satisfaction. Improving oneself is not trying to become perfect but to reach that level of satisfaction from within. Exaggerated praise and rewards are in the end counterproductive.

Self-control is required to control movement but also the mind and the will. In Children’s House there are two exercises related to this tendency: walking on the line and the silence game. The ability of self-control is linked to learning to obey oneself. The minimum rules that are in the Children’s House are very challenging for the young children but are also important to help them develop self-control. If you can control yourself you gain patience.

To communicate – mainly with others, this is all done almost always through language. We don’t know when spoken language emerged but we consider it a characteristic of our language (articulated language). Articulated language require a special apparatus but also the mind capacity to articulate and abstract.

The advantages of communication are: passing knowledge from one to another, organise ourselves and work in a collaborative way. If we organize ourselves we can work as one. It has been of crucial importance for the survival of the specie. After some time we passed from spoken language to written language as soon as the groups increased in size. The children are capable to acquire this ability long before they will need this instruments as adults. We use language to communicate with ourselves when thinking, language comes also as means of self-expression. Language is a very deep and innate characteristic of the human beings.

children.title: To associate: to associate with others

blocks.text: Human beings are social beings, we always lived in groups. For the right development of the child he needs to develop in a group. Jean Marc Gaspard Hard (1788 -1828) found a wild boy in the French woods (Aveyron) and called him Victor. After a certain period of time Victor made some improvements but he never could adapt to society completely or communicate more than a few words. Human environment is mandatory for the development of the person and so is the association with the other human beings. Children have to grow up in association with other human beings. The first plane children are especially attracted to the adults, we can say as well that they like the company of the other children. In Children’s House the children form bonds of affection which is called social cohesion by Maria Montessori. From the years 3 to 6 Maria Montessori talks about a society embryo. This is a very important time for the formation of character. For the flourishing of the social values it is important to have a mix age community. For the second plane children they tent to associate with their friends and peers instead of the family. At this moment of their life they like to form groups and to work together. We expect the children to collaborate, share work and share ideas. It’s a practice society. For the adolescents they become involved in the adult’s society to the extent of even bringing an economic value to the community. They need to associate and to work together as a whole. It would not be important to create a supernature without of the tendency to associate and work in groups.

In conclusion all these tendencies work together and manifest themselves over the whole life. They have a crucial importance during the course of the history from the first human being to the humanity today.
While working with the children it is important to have in mind not only the sensitivities, the characteristics of the plane but also the tendencies. While observing it is important

to observe these tendencies and the lack of some might point out situation to investigate to see if it’s normal. (E.g. no exploration in the classroom). All the human tendencies work together and not in isolation.

children.title: Review of the four planes development

blocks.text: For animals we can think of a pattern of developemnt that it is specific for a specie but for the humans we can think of individual patterns. This is the reason why any causalistic approach cannot work – the individual should be allowed to develop according to his individual pattern. The adult cannot be the creator of the child, the child is not something to be molded or filled instead we have to see the children as a human being that should be respected and just aided in her process of development if required avoiding to help more than necessary. The period from 0 to 18 years old can be viewed as a start of a new life. The four planes of development are identified by Maria Montessori as:

 0 – 6 years old [First plane]: Infancy  6-12 years old [Second plane]: Childhood  12-18 years old [Third plane]: Adolescence  18-24 years olf [Forth plane]: Maturity The first and the third plane of development can be also called “self-construction” planes. The first plane of the development can be split in a three-fold:  Human being who is developing  Human being who is adapting  Human being who is an unique individual

In the first part of the first plane of development, the sensitivies are peaking and in the second part are slowly fading. Maria Montessori calls the child of the first subplane an “Unconscious creator” because the child creates a human being. The child of the second plane of development is called a “Conscious worker/explorer”. It is the second subplane is when the consciousness is developing. The child is doing a work of perfectionment at this time, a perfectionment of the senses, movement and language.

The nature gives to the child the absorbment mind and lots of creative energy in order to succesfully do the work of development required in this stage of their life. The absorbment mind it is called by Maria unconscius absorbment mind during the first 3 years of life and consciuous absorbment mind in the next three years of life (3-6 years old).

We can think of the each passage from a plane of development to the other as rebirths of the child and each has to be lived at its fullest if the nature’s goal is to be achieved. If the natural development is supported the individual will reach optimal development. Every plane of development of has its contributions to make.

The goal or finality of the development is to create an independent adult, but in each plane a stage of independence it is reached. The adult society it is an interdependent network of exchange and interchange. The adult has to be able to function as an independent individual in this interdependent society.

In education the whole individual has to be taken in account not only the intellectual aspect – it has to be holistic approach. A healthy society cannot be achieved only by taking care of the intellect.

When talking about the acquisition of culture Maria Montessori talked about the acquisition of knowledge to understand the world in which they are living.
“Our experience with children in elementary schools has shown us that the age between 6 and 12 years is a period of live during each all the elements of all
sciences should be given. It is a period that might be called the sensitive period for culture. During which the abstract plane of the human is organized” Maria Montessori

“At this age it is possible for the child to take in an enormous amount of culture. We have found by experience that during this period the syllabus has to be enlarged containing not only the knowledge from the primary period but many things taught
in the succeeding secondary period. “Maria Montessori
The strong legs of the child in the second plane of development symbolize the need of a larger environment for the child and an intellectual need for exploration.
In contrast to the young child who is happy in a small environment, the child in elementary seeks for an environment which is larger, wider that can answer to its hunger for knowledge and answers.
The powers created and perfected by the younger child can be used during the childhood plane to satisfy his hunger for knowledge.

The second plane child develops an ability to picture a reality that he cannot see it physically around him, an ability to experience what is inaccessible to the senses. The older child is still seeking reality, but the only way to see, picture and experience the reality at the level of the world, universe is the imagination. Only in this way he can develop a sense of belonging to a whole world and become a citizen of “La Nazione Unica” (the single nation of humanity).
This reality is very different from the reality of the younger child. This kind of adaptation is called a second phase of adaption.
“What gave a great joy to the children was to realize clearly how the world functions in his physical phenomena (distribution of heat, air currents, sea currents, rain,

erosion, deposition, etc.); how different plants and animals distributed themselves according to conditions and how humanity fitted in this context. The vision on a higher level of this far larger environment of the possibility following their present tendencies to absorb it formed a second phase in the process that the human individual undergoes to achieve adaption. The miracle of the child who assimilates and adapts to an environment that he can only imagine. Although the second plane of development is not a creative one, the knowledge acquired during this

Imagination
“Imagination is the great power of this age, a sort of sensitive period for the imagination exists in the second plane of development” Maria Montessori

We can call the imagination during the first six years of live as reproductive imagination. The child can imagine things that he has already seen. A lot of work that is done in the first plane of development is done to help the child reach abstraction. The imagination serves the tendency to abstract.
The kind imagination that the children older than six years old also possess, beside the reproductive imagination, can be called creative imagination. With the help of this
imagination they can combine different abstract concepts to imagine something new that they have never seen.

There are different orders of abstraction (E.g. “table”, “red”) and all these levels can serve the child in the second plane of development to imagine concepts that he has never seen/thought of before.
“Creative imagination enables us to …. “ Camilo Grazzini

Creative imagination is at work also when the mind uses the abstract real concepts already known to bring in to reality things that never existed. These abstract real concepts that we know are called by Maria Montessori: “the alphabet of imagination”.
Tendency to associate (Social aspects of the second plane child)
The humans are social by nature, there is a human tendency to associate. The human presence and power on the planet comes from this tendency to associate which helped humanity to thrive.

In the first plane of development the children tend to associate with the close members of the family. The Children’s House it is a society by cohesion which is held together by the feelings of the children for the others (affection, kindness, etc.)

With the second plane of development the children want to associate, work and collaborate with their peers. There is a shift of interest from the family towards the friends and colleagues. They are interested in having rules, creating that rules and imposing them for their “pretend society” - “little democracies”. The children create these groups spontaneously. The children will choose leaders in their groups in an active or passive way.
Morality

Morality comes into play from living with others. Morality has everything to do with society. Each human being has its physical territory as well as their spiritual territory which includes (religion, behaviour, custom, morality). The spiritual territory is describing a certain group of people and their set of values. The children born in that group will slowly unconsciously incarnate these values that the group has. The older child of the second plane will question everything, all the aspects accepted before.

The children will develop their own code of morality in their strive for independency. The children will try to understand the code of morality used by the adults of his group but not at any cost, the child might decide for himself if something is right or not using the power of compassion, so powerful in the young children (E.g. Maria Montessori’s example with the goat and the child).

With the cosmic education the children learn of the value of the different forms of work, by all forms of nature, by all forms of life. The children are helped to become aware of the importance of the value of work, collaboration and cosmic work. The
children develop a cosmic morality, which is respect and gratitude towards life and mankind.
“Man is conscious of his own intellectual and physical needs and the claims on him of and society. He is fighting for himself, family and nation but yet to be conscious of
this deeper cosmic task, collaborations, work with others for the whole universe” Maria Montessori

With the cosmic education it is presented the whole, starting with the biggest whole: the universe. This is done with the cosmic fables and stories – these are called “Stories of truth” by Mario Montessori. These stories have an emphasis on reality and come to answer part of the questions that the children might have. The stories are offered as a help for the second plane children, these stories provides the seeds that can grow with the children.

If the children have lived the first two planes of development well, they will become learners for life and they were never be limited by what the teacher knows. The second plane of development contributes in creating an adult which is fully responsible socially, sensitive and responsible in the relationship with the Earth and the mankind.
“The secret of good teaching is to regard the child’s intelligence as a fertile field in which seeds may be sown, to grow under the heat of flaming imagination. Our aim
therefore is not merely to make the child understand, and still less to force him to memorise, but so to touch his imagination as to enthuse him to his inmost core. We

do not want complacent pupils, but eager ones; we seek to sow life in the child rather than theories, to help him in his growth, mental and emotional as well as physical, and for that we must offer grand and lofty ideas to the human mind, which
we find ever ready to receive them …” Maria Montessori – To educate the human potential

It is not enough for the teacher to love the child, now the teacher has to love the world. The teacher has to become a “story teller of the truth”. He has to help the children in their social and individual development such that they can become adults.

The second plane of developments is the one is the plane that prepares the children for the tasks of responsibility. The responsibility can be divided in a social responsibility, moral responsibility and a cosmic responsibility.
To have responsibility it is very important to offer freedom so that responsibility can develop.

If in the first plane the children want to do things for themselves in the second plane the children are interested to think for themselves. The activities of the first plane help the child to develop the responsibility that it is required later in the second plane to fully enjoy their freedom. The freedom mentioned is the freedom necessary to develop according to one’s potential and not a complete freedom without any rules.

The freedom in the classroom in the Children’s House it is a freedom to make choices and to move in the environment. In the first years of life freedom and discipline are interconnected and one without the other is not possible. One can think of freedom and discipline as being one thing in the first plane of development. The freedom most adults think about children it is a not imposing any limits therefore it is associated with chaos. Later in the first years of school the freedom of movement is associated with the recess time and the freedom of choice becomes a reward for being obedient and following the indications of the adults.

Freedom in the Montessori Education it is given in the context of the prepared environment where the child can make choices that guide him towards his own development. If given the knowledge and guided properly the child can benefit of the freedom to develop fully.

In the Children’s House the discipline is there to help the child in making good choices within the freedom offered. In the general context discipline is thought of as a capacity to obey blindly the instructions of the other members of society (Discipline is defined in the dictionary as the practice of training people to obey rules or a code of behaviour, using punishment to correct disobedience). In the Montessori context discipline is connected to one’s self-control and capacity of making choices for themselves. Discipline can be seen as an interior order of the individual this is why the discipline requires freedom to be obtained and at the same time the freedom requires one’s self discipline.

In a prepared environment the children can freely choose activities that attract them and guide them towards working with interest and concentration and this leads towards a spontaneous discipline. Having the freedom and the discipline the independence it is fostered in the children.

For every freedom in the environment should be a limit mutually agreed by the adults and the children so that the child can feel secure to explore and make choices with responsibility. In this exercise of creating oneself, the children should feel comfortable
to make mistakes and should have the tools to correct their mistakes without this becoming an event in which he is pointed out.
